newsitem.title: USA: CCC buys 32,380 tonnes grains at N.Korean tender.
newsitem.headline: CCC buys 32,380 tonnes grains at N.Korean tender.

text.p: The Commodity Credit Corp of the U.S. Department of Agriculture said it purchased a total of 32,380 tonnes of commodities under an invitation for supplies for export to North Korea.
It bought 20,780 tonnes of U.S. yellow corn, 5,000 tonnes of corn/soy blend and 6,600 tonnes of milled rice.
A spokeswoman for the CCC could not confirm the purchase was for North Korea although the original invitation stated it as the destination.
The corn purchase comprised 16,180 tonnes from Cargill Inc priced between $153.15 and $160.24 a tonne and 4,600 tonnes from ADM/Growmark at $156.81 a tonne, FOB.
The rice purchase comprised 5,600 tonnes from Continental Grain at between $374.79 and $379.94 a tonne and 1,000 tonnes from Gulf Pacific Rice Co at $375.00 a tonne, FOB.
The corn/soy blend purchase was from Lauhoff Grain and priced between $334.21 and $335.32 a tonne, FOB.
The commodities were for shipment before April 1.
Earlier this month the United States formally announced an extra $10 million in food aid for North Korea, considerably more than originally expected and above last year's donation of $6.4 million.
